answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by pricing identity through a stake only sustained work accrues. Each agent locks a bond from an escrowed uptime record before it may vote or attest, and vouching peers raise that bond. Forging a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds plus a thousand independent checks, so identity one and identity one-thousand cost alike. Clones scan the horizon and find no cheap path: each fake peer must earn the same history, and one failed attestation brings a gale of slashing that erases the stake. No swarm reaches the summit of majority without burning lost capital.
